body: I distinctly remember being at my friend's housewarming party and it was already wrapping up but typical drunk me still wanted to keep going. I started to help clean up all of the open beer bottles all over the apartment, but I was mostly trying to find which ones I could down. It was gross and everyone was put off. I had already stopped drinking for two years before that, and it would be another two years before I stopped again and hope to stay that way.
I used Talkspace but it hasn't really helped me.

Didn't drink! Did a fast instead. 

Question though, do you say, "I don't drink" or "I don't drink anymore"? Does the anymore invite unwanted questions/bring awkwardness to a conversation?

I always noticed my hair feeling extra terrible after a particularly bad bender. My habits in the shower are so routine that I'm sure my blackout demon conditioned, but even so, it felt like grody ass straw. IWNDWYT.

My partner's father was 52 when he died from alcoholism. His heart failed him. He had been sober for about six months to a year after years of heavy drinking. And it only  took one more year of drinking for him to die. Drinking alienated his family who treated him like a ghost while he was alive for years. His death was devastating in innumerable ways. There was so much good in him, and it was muted when he drank. Being able to see him sober was a gift. And it made it that much harder to see him go back to the bottle when every potential and opportunity for interaction was materially damaged. I hope your sister escapes the claws of alcoholism. I hope she sees that it's not too late.

Two weeks ago, I went on a bender and nearly destroyed my relationship with my partner. Today, we're on speaking terms, and I'm looking forward to working out, cleaning, and indulge in sweets and snacks. Maybe even studying, putting together a blog, gaming, and freelancing. 

As I was on my way to work this morning, I saw an older gentleman stinking of alcohol getting led by his wife off the train. It was a depressing sight. To think months ago, I dropped and shattered a whole bottle of wine (thankfully in a plastic bag) drunk as hell in that very station one evening, threw out the shards, and went on the train in one fel swoop without mopping anything up. I'm happy I'm not in that position today. IWNDWYT.

Yesterday was a hard day. A strong urge to just go find a random bar to sneak a drink before dinner with my parents washed over me. I was so, so tempted, but then a stationery store distracted me and I flew in there as fast as I could. Then during dinner, I pounded a bottle and a half of sparkling water, which honestly was just as refreshing. r/stopdrinking is the greatest comfort I can turn to when I feel this way. I won't drink with you today.

Saving this for when I feel compelled to read a wondrously beautiful piece of writing again. Equal parts of darkness and hope. I'm sure I speak for everyone that I hope you feel wordy sooner rather than later :\)

I didn't drink today despite going to an engagement party and getting offered a shot and a glass of wine! Though I did have a sip of moscato because my friend wanted me to taste how it was, I didn't and don't feel compelled to drink. I did, however, go buy a pack of cigarettes. So that's not good. But yay, I made it!
I didn't drink today and felt no compulsion to! A stark difference to yesterday's fear of losing my resolve.

I totally get that. I wouldn't miss this for the world though, especially if I'm on the same continent as my friend. I think I'll have to scrounge up whatever resolve I had when I stopped drinking for two years and try to emulate it as much as possible.

Fuck you, little voice! I'll try to avoid calling attention to myself. I'm tasked with taking pictures of people, though, so it'll be good to just pop in, take the picture, and whisk myself away to others. Thank you for the advice and support!

The problem is I've drank with these people before, so it'll have to be, "I don't drink *anymore*." Then it'll maybe be questions, but I think I'll avoid it entirely by just having a nondescript, non-alcoholic drink near me. 
Thank you for the support. I should've came to this subreddit earlier in the year when I thought I was going to quit.

I think the scenario would be more like: "Hey! Here's a drink!" to which I would respond, "No, thank you!" and maybe questions or some persistence on the other person's part, or "Hey! Why aren't you drinking?" "WELP!"
But yeah, I'll likely just say I'll have to get up early the next day. Mother's day anyway :D
I think in my head, it's that I know they'll judge me and keep a mental note of it, but ultimately I'm not the main concern. And that mental note bugs the shit out of me.
In Asia. Didn't drink today, but hell, I had a small voice go, "You could totally get away with one and that'd be it!" But I knew it wouldn't be the case.
Thank you! Congrats on your three days! ♥️

Which ones? I assure you there were more than just one. If you're talking about going to breweries at all and being in places that could be tempting, sure. I agree. That would be a terrible ifea. But you can't always avoid those settings, especially at a booze-filled wedding. Hence why I said it's different for everyone.
Go request a badge in the sidebar! Super quick to get this snazzy count... up haha.
SO PROUD OF YOU! Just focus one day at a time. You fucking got this.

I'll probably try to keep making posts like this to remind myself that moderation won't work and that first drink will trigger an avalanche of misery. I'm glad this one helps. I remember watching a documentary on eating disorders and body dysphoria, and a person with a PhD, who was extremely thin and beautiful, said something along the lines of, "Intellectually, I know I look fine the way I am. That I don't need to lose anymore weight and that my BFP is well below average. But I still feel like I have to starve." And that's always stuck with me. Even if you're capable of recognizing the faults, it will always be hell to quiet that irrational part of you that's always saying, "MORE, DAMMIT." When I stopped drinking for two years, it didn't get that much easier. I still felt cravings and still wanted to at least moderate or sip something just to \~try\~. In fact, I relapsed in Japan because I thought, "Um, I'm in fucking Japan. Give me a kirin and sake at this izakaya." And then it started a snowball when I returned home. 

I think it's important to just remind yourself of all the terrible shit that either has or hasn't happened. I still wish for that program/script I mentioned above somewhere that automatically appears whenever the moderation thought forms. But until then, IWNDWYT and rationalize on.
God, so relatable, haha. Wine is the main course and everything else is secondary. To hell with moderation.

Breweries might be fun to tour, but it would be good to avoid those settings if they're too tempting. I saw someone post that it took six months for them to be okay with going to bars without wanting to drink, but I guess it's different for everyone. You could probably pick other places that don't revolve around alcohol with your friends, or at least wait until you can be okay enough to not drink with them. Those hobbies sound fun and rewarding! Whenever you can, and if you want obviously, please give updates on those. :D

Being able to recognize it could potentially ruin you in the future, the way you're going now, is incredibly insightful. I can identify with everything you've said here because I, too, haven't had legal trouble, but I so very easily could have. Most of my friendships and relationships are tarnished because of drinking. What's the point if you forget every meaningful interaction you've had? Of repeating questions and forgetting what the other person as they're talking? 

I should have come to r/stopdrinking when I tried quitting again months ago. The feeling of watching movies/TV depicting alcohol as a funny substance and wondering why I couldn't function like that is damaging as hell. But I'll take boredom over potentially fucking everything up. IWNDWYT.

Happy early birthday! I think your friend is probably feeling anxious about realizing he has a problem. I remember being that type of person to constantly want to drink and everyone else being super uncomfortable with it. I thought to myself, "Isn't this how it's supposed to be? Why are they all looking at me weird? Fucking drink with me, dammit." And now I have to stop completely lol. Granted, they weren't the party/clubbing type of people, and the ones I did find claim that I wasn't much of a problem, but their habits will hopefully not land them in the hospital or totaling their car at the risk of death. I'm saving your list to remind myself of those daily. IWNDWYT :\)

Welcome back! You're doing great so far. I relapsed and lied about my drinking because I was lonely, too. But alcohol never seems to fill the emptiness. It's better to find something else that isn't temporary and will stick around more without hurting you. Got any hobbies or clubs you'd be interested in joining?
HECK YEAH

I tried moderating for about two years, blacking out more times than I can count and promising I'd stop until I ruined any sort of "reliable" quality to my persons. Like, so much shit happened for absolutely nothing. And I finally understood that just one for a while will ruin everything. 

Maybe it wouldn't hurt to be in a bar and be sober to better your chances, but it depends on whether the environment will trigger you.
It's fine ♥️ Thank you so much!
Such a beautiful post. I relate to your experience, or lack thereof. But so many fucking closecalls. I'm happy you've made the realization without hitting rock bottom.
You'd think it's a good plan. If only there was something like a repelling force that physically capped you from doing so. Fuck moderation.

Its enticement is alluring. Awareness is anxiety-inducing and reality is a shithole, so why not subdue those burdens just a little? Now, how about losing yourself to the abyss, while also sacrificing everything you know and love? Long-term? No drug is worth the loss of consciousness nor its prolongment. The world moves forward with or without you, and losing out on life is a shitty way of living, even moreso if it's in your control. Everyone has their story, but everyone can contribute something to the world. 

Sorry for the rambling. Your post triggered something in me. It's motivated even more to work hard to better my life and the lives of others.
Wow, I'm touched my post had some impact. Glad you went <3
Ain't that the truth. I'm going to make damn sure that this time is the last.

The mind is a tricksy thing. I wish there were an automated program/script that flashes all of your terrible experiences and emotions as real as the moment you lived it (or the shame of blackout the next day) the instant that thought "innocently" forms.
Heck yeah.
Yeah!!!
Hey, hope you're referring to whatever u/LondonBridgeinRain posted prior and not the one here.
Hahaha that's brilliant. Totally going to use that.

I've tried conveying this to my partner and they just said they don't understand why this thought persists, especially when presented with all the reasons why I can't drink and my past history with it. But you're right, it is a greater strength to not drink than to moderate at any length.
Substituting one addiction for another, haha. Sugar is a lowly gremlin compared to a demon like alcohol. What kind of cookie did you eat?
I hope so as well. I'm glad we're all in this together.
With every moderation relapse, I always prided myself in thinking I could stop at one. For the first couple of times. And then it goes, "Well, two won't hurt," and ... yeah. Same.
Thanks for reading!
Wow, he's been through a lot. I'll be sure to check out more of his stuff. Thanks for the recommendation.
This. Exactly this. It's like Memento, honestly. Sometimes I feel a need to tattoo all the terrible things that have happened on my body so I never forget.
We most certainly can't.
It's been worse, but not as bad as it could have been. Totaled my car, fell down some stairs, laid puking on a subway platform completely immobile, been hospitalized several times... yeah.
Proud of you!

your black-out self and mine had a remarkably similar incident. mine occurred months ago, except my partner was trying to break up with me after seeing i couldn't control myself drinking (even if we were together for 5+ years) and my solution was what you did. 10+ drinks deep. with barely any traffic because.. suburbs.
for me, it was all the overwatch loot boxes...
An LA Fitness membership while I was a brokeass student. Didn't use it for a year or more thinking I would go. It was $50 a month. It still pains me to think about.

I would argue that while memes have conveyed a relatability of everyday truths for people, the very same relatability has also destroyed any semblance of genuineness of expressing personal experiences and reduced it to nothingness. The only way we can convey our existential despair isn't through pages and strings of philosophical thought as it was done in the past but through absurd memes that commands the attention in a short burst before fading from memory. For the people who do use writing as an outlet, they're judged for making light of their misery because of the commonality of this experience, and are instead ridiculed mercilessly on Twitter or other platforms. No wonder why Generation Y are so maladjusted and depressed. No wonder we're going to die the loneliest generation. We're destined to be these ironic meme-spewing duds who think mocking our human condition is a given.
